One-sentence judgment: calculate, classify, record, and check basic financial data to produce complete and traceable accounting records. In the United States this corresponds to 43-3031.00, Bright Outlook, Job Zone Three; this does not mean employment growth is positive. Bookkeeping clerk status does not automatically confer accounting supervisor status, external filing signature authority, or statutory audit qualifications; the responsibility of the unit's person in charge does not exempt the handling personnel from responsibility.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to check the original vouchers and the business facts clearly before entering them; you can accept that the same transaction is reviewed repeatedly, aiming for "vouchers matching the books, books matching each other" rather than "just finish entering it"; when numbers do not match, the account to use is doubtful, or deadlines conflict, you are willing to stop and report first rather than adjust the numbers to make the surface balance; and your interest in "can this record stand up to review" is greater than in "how many entries I made today".

Pause before making a large investment: if you do not yet understand debits and credits, accounts, periods, and bank reconciliation, start with the BK-01 paper exercise on this page and check it against clear inputs and a reference answer. Completing the exercise or a software course does not prove that you can independently handle real unit closing, filing, or statutory audits; practical work still requires position training, authority, and review arrangements.

The U.S. BLS lists the typical entry-level education as some college, no degree, with moderate-term on-the-job training; employer requirements vary, some accept a high school diploma, and professional certification is usually not required. In the O*NET education question, 41% chose high school or equivalent, 21% chose a postsecondary certificate, and 12% chose a bachelor's degree; these are respondents' answers about the education required for the position, not the educational composition of workers or a uniform statutory threshold. Accounting personnel in mainland China must have the professional competence required by the position; the head of an accounting office or the accounting supervisor must additionally hold a professional technical position qualification at the accountant level or above, or have more than three years of experience in accounting work. Continuing education applies to those who hold an accounting professional technical qualification and to those who work in accounting without that qualification, starting in the year after obtaining the qualification or starting work; it is no fewer than 90 credit hours per year, with professional subjects generally no less than two-thirds, and the specific registration follows local rules. It cannot be presumed applicable from all office clerk titles.

One sentence: this is a support finance position centered on voucher checking, account classification, posting and reconciliation, assistance with statement preparation, and record archiving, and its output is accurate, timely, reviewable accounting records rather than an audit opinion or a tax or legal conclusion. The U.S. wage, employment, and projection data are the precise occupational basis for Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks (SOC 43-3031); mainland China has no national occupational-level wage statistics corresponding to this occupation, and this page shows only verifiable proxy bases and the gap.

The work of this occupation can be divided into three categories: first, day-to-day accounting processing (checking original vouchers, coding by account and company procedure, entering the journal and general ledger, posting and summarizing debits and credits, and maintaining receivables, payables, and inventory records); second, checking and settlement (checking amounts and postings, finding and reporting differences, bank reconciliation, preparing deposit and payment vouchers, and preparing a trial balance); third, support and filing (preparing invoices and statements, organizing cost and budget data, filling in tax and social insurance forms, and preparing statistical and financial reports for others to review). All three share the same traceable chain of evidence.
Day-to-day accounting processing

Obtain the original voucher → determine the nature of the transaction and the period it belongs to → code by account and company procedure → enter the journal → post to the general or subsidiary ledger → summarize debits and credits and check the balance → archive vouchers and records.
Checking and settlement

Check amounts, postings, and document coding → compare bank statements with book records item by item → when a difference is found, record it, trace it, and report it → prepare deposit, payment, and invoice vouchers → prepare a trial balance and reconciliation notes → keep review traces.

Issue invoices and statements according to established procedures, organize cost, budget, and expense data, fill in forms for taxes, social insurance, and pensions, prepare statistics and financial reports related to receivables, payables, and profit and loss, and hand the basic data to accountants, finance supervisors, or auditors for review and use.

This occupation centers on accounting records and checking: accountants and auditors (13-2011.00) apply accounting standards, prepare statements, and make audit judgments, and are responsible for the conclusions; financial managers (11-3031.00) handle funds, budgets, and decisions; credit analysts and loan officers focus on credit and lending assessment; tax examiners and revenue agents represent tax authorities in enforcement; and billing and posting clerks and payroll and timekeeping clerks focus on receivables billing and payroll accounting respectively. Similar position titles do not mean responsibilities are interchangeable.
Core purpose
Make every economic transaction accurately recorded by voucher, account, and period, so that financial records are complete, checkable, and traceable.
Main objects and basis

The objects are original vouchers, invoices and receipt and payment documents, journals and general ledgers, bank statements, and receivables, payables, and inventory records; the basis is accounting standards and the unit's accounting system, internal approval and coding procedures, and tax and employment filing requirements.
Core process

Voucher checking, account determination and coding, entry and posting, summarization and trial balance, bank and account reconciliation, difference tracing and reporting, assistance with statement preparation, and record archiving.
Main outputs
Accurate and timely journal and general ledger records, reconciliation and difference notes, invoices and statements, trial balances, and basic financial and statistical reports available for review.
Responsible party

In mainland China, the person in charge of a unit bears responsibility for the accounting work and the truthfulness and completeness of the materials, while the handling personnel still perform accounting and supervision duties according to law. Reports that by law must be audited by certified public accountants are issued by certified public accountants and their accounting firms under the rules; internal audit, government inspection, and bookkeeping support each have their own duties and are not collectively called a certified public accountant's signature.
Authority and approval

Whether you can post independently, adjust already-recorded entries, or provide financial data or filing materials externally is determined by the unit's authorization and internal approval process, and does not arise by itself from proficiency or software permissions.
Boundary of conclusions

Accounting records state that "under the existing vouchers and procedures, this transaction has been recorded and checked"; they do not mean the financial report has been approved, nor do they replace audit, tax, or legal judgment, and they are affected by voucher completeness, period attribution, and account determination.

Before starting the job, check at least six items: the position basis and the nature of the unit, the education and training path, the software and account set actually used, the approval authority for posting and adjustments, data confidentiality and access control requirements, and the real method of pay and work hour arrangements.
Occupational basis

Insufficient evidence: no same-basis Chinese occupational wage or employment distribution was obtained. This page uses the U.S. O*NET-SOC 43-3031.00 occupational classification; in mainland China, check against the specific accounting work, the nature of the unit, the organizational form, and the position duties, and bookkeeping, cashier work, accounting supervision, and statutory audit cannot be interchanged on the basis of the title alone. This page does not claim a one-to-one correspondence between Chinese and U.S. occupational categories.
Education and training path

The U.S. BLS lists the typical entry-level education as some college, no degree, with moderate-term on-the-job training; employer requirements vary, some accept a high school diploma, and professional certification is usually not required. In the O*NET education question, 41% chose high school or equivalent, 21% chose a postsecondary certificate, and 12% chose a bachelor's degree; these are respondents' answers about the education required for the position, not the educational composition of workers or a uniform statutory threshold.
Methods and tools

The details page lists 28 software categories; the Hot single page lists 19 products and 5 In-Demand: Excel31%, QuickBooks21%, Office19%, Outlook10%, SAP6%; Word4%, PowerPoint2%, Concur/PeopleSoft1%, and another 8 items below 1%, while Project/Oracle Database are not published and are not filled in as 0. The denominator is unique U.S. job postings in 2025, not an adoption rate, a required skill, or an AI substitution rate.
Data and confidentiality

Accounting data involves sensitive content such as the unit's business information and individual pay; check the access permissions, modification audit trail, and backup mechanisms of the account set and data, confirm whether cloud services or third-party tools are allowed to process these data, and verify the approval process for providing data externally.
Records and review

In mainland China, Article 4 of the Accounting Law (amended in 2024) makes the person in charge of the unit responsible for the truthfulness and completeness of the unit's accounting work and materials; Article 14 requires checking original vouchers, returning inaccurate or incomplete records for correction or supplementation, and requiring the issuing unit to reissue those with amount errors; Article 25 provides that bookkeeping, approval, handling, and custody of property duties are separated and mutually constrained; and Article 35 prohibits a cashier from concurrently serving as the checker, the keeper of accounting archives, and the registrar of revenue, expenditure, expense, and claims and debt accounts. Editorial suggestion: set up review, version, and change notes together with unit rules, and do not conclude that the accounting is correct merely because the balances are equal.
Pay and work hours

The same position title may be paid monthly, hourly, or by piece, and is affected by overtime brought by closing cycles, tax filing periods, and annual audits; when comparing, put the software and account set permissions, whether you bear external filing responsibility, overtime and compensatory time arrangements, and continuing education costs into the written agreement.

Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks (U.S. side O*NET-SOC 43-3031.00) compute, classify, and record numerical data to keep financial records complete; they perform routine calculating, posting, and checking duties to obtain the primary financial data used to maintain accounting records; they may also check the accuracy of figures, calculations, and postings of business transactions recorded by other workers. It is not a financial decision-making position, and the official definition does not automatically grant the authority to sign audit opinions or tax conclusions; holding other positions concurrently requires checking that jurisdiction's qualifications and responsibilities separately.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET-SOC 43-3031.00 Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks, Bright Outlook, updated 2026, Job Zone Three (SVP 6.0 to <7.0). The official duties are to "compute, classify, and record numerical data to keep financial records complete"; there are 28 tasks in total (13 Core, 15 Supplemental), and the highly important tasks include using accounting software to record and analyze information (94), checking figures, postings, and documents for correct entry, mathematical accuracy, and proper coding (92), complying with federal, state, and company policies and procedures (89), using calculators and photocopy equipment to complete calculations and prepare documents (87), and receiving, recording, and depositing cash, checks, and vouchers (87).

U.S. wage distribution: the 2025 BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) presented by O*NET, on the basis of this precise occupation (Bookkeeping, Accounting, and Auditing Clerks, SOC 43-3031) — annual wage 10th percentile 36,000 USD, 25th percentile 43,520 USD, median 50,670 USD, 75th percentile 61,470 USD, and 90th percentile 74,550 USD; the corresponding median hourly wage is 24.36 USD.

NBS2025 matching reference (pre-tax annual average, yuan/year): leasing and business services, urban non-private 110,162 and private 68,919, above designated size all 92,849, clerical personnel 88,460, and professional and technical personnel 149,542; financial sector non-private 211,164 and private 140,451; wholesale and retail 135,749 and 69,622, above designated size all 112,030, clerical 97,096, and professional and technical 140,999. Choose according to the actual employer industry and your own duties; professional accounting may fall under professional and technical personnel, and the U.S. Clerk translation alone cannot be used to classify all of them as clerical personnel. The cross-industry above-designated-size all 106,080 and clerical 94,936 still serve only as background, not as an occupational median or starting salary. Precise national occupational wages and city monthly wages remain insufficient evidence.

Both the current O*NET and BLS use 2025—2035: employment 1,532,400 → 1,446,800, a decline of 6%, with a BLS net decrease of 85,600, and the 144,100 annual openings all come from replacement needs after transfers or exits, not net additions, a hiring guarantee, or a causal estimate attributable to generative AI alone.

O*NET2025 U.S. 43-3031.00 industry distribution: professional, scientific, and technical services 14%, other 86% (including construction, health care, and social assistance). This is a U.S. industry attribution, not a wage explanation, a Chinese industry, or an individual employer classification.

paragraphs: This page compares bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and output, key differences, and which direction suits each preference. The adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupational descriptions and do not mean the position titles are interchangeable.

Evidence note: the career directions and core outputs are based on the official descriptions of O*NET 43-3031.00 and related occupation lists and are on the U.S. basis; the qualification, licensing, and authorization requirements of adjacent occupations must be verified separately by their own jurisdiction, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut to a career change.

The table below compares bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks with adjacent occupations and the paths for moving in from adjacent positions; the basis for judgment is the main output, what the role is responsible for, and the training required, rather than how similar the occupational titles are.
Accountants and Auditors (13-2011.00)

Accountants and auditors may prepare, analyze, or review financial records, perform audit procedures, and present findings and recommendations; not every accounting position issues an audit opinion, and the conditions for signing a statutory audit must be checked separately by jurisdiction.

Both handle accounting data, but accountants and auditors bear responsibility for applying standards, preparing statements, and making audit judgments; bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks center on the recording accuracy of vouchers, postings, and reconciliation, and usually do not sign statements or audit opinions.

If you want to bear responsibility for standards judgment and audit conclusions, look first at accountants and auditors; if you would rather make basic accounting accurate and checkable, look first at the bookkeeping and accounting clerk direction.
Billing and Posting Clerks (43-3021.00)
Focused on accounts receivable billing, amount checking, and posting, with billing and collection records as the main output.

Billing and posting clerks concentrate more on the billing and receivables link; bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks cover broader day-to-day accounting, reconciliation, and assistance with statement preparation.

If you would rather focus on billing and receivables processes, compare billing and posting clerks first; if you want to cover a more complete accounting chain, look first at the bookkeeping and accounting clerk direction.
Payroll and Timekeeping Clerks (43-3051.00)
Calculate work hours and pay, handle withholding and remittance and disbursement, with payroll tables and related filings as the main output.

Payroll and timekeeping clerks focus on work hours, pay, and related withholding; bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks cover broader accounting and checking, and some positions also handle payroll, so it cannot be asserted that the two never overlap.

If you are more interested in pay and employment data, compare payroll and timekeeping clerks first; if you would rather do general accounting and reconciliation, look first at the bookkeeping and accounting clerk direction.
Credit Analysts (13-2041.00)
Assess the credit risk of borrowers and customers, with credit analysis and lending recommendations as the main output.

Credit analysts center on risk judgment and lending recommendations and need financial analysis and judgment skills; bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks center on recording accuracy and checking, and usually do not make lending judgments.
If you would rather do risk assessment and judgment, look first at credit analysts; if you would rather make basic data accurate, look first at the bookkeeping and accounting clerk direction.
Financial Managers (11-3031.00)
Responsible for funds, budgets, investment and financing, and managing the finance team, and responsible for financial decisions and external reporting.

Financial managers bear decision-making and management responsibility and need longer experience and a broader financial perspective; bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks provide reviewable basic data and do not bear funds and budget decisions.

If you want to bear funds and budget decision responsibility, you must first build experience and make up management capabilities; if you would rather go deep and be accurate at the accounting level, look first at the bookkeeping and accounting clerk direction.
Moving in from administrative, cashier, or data entry positions
You already have document processing, customer communication, or data entry experience and want to move to standardized accounting work.

The gap is usually not typing or software operation but accounting accounts and debit and credit logic, period attribution, reconciliation and difference handling, and confidentiality and approval discipline; knowing how to enter data does not mean knowing how to keep books.

If you are willing to make up accounting fundamentals and checking training and accept review, you can consider moving in; if you only want a different position title without understanding the business and the accounts, the gap will be large.

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the main output, what the role is responsible for, and the training required, not how similar the names are; once the direction is set, check the education and examination requirements of the target direction, the software and account set actually used, the approval authority for posting and adjustments, and the external filing responsibility item by item, and keep written confirmation.

paragraphs: Students or career changers preparing to enter this occupation

Start with the BK-01 fictional exercise on this page, then check whether the target position is enterprise finance, agency bookkeeping, public institution finance, or a shared service center, and confirm the training, accounting system, and authorization arrangements for each. The paper exercise does not require existing internship experience or a mentor.
Practicing bookkeeping and accounting clerks

Editorial task analysis: use generative tools in reviewable links such as voucher information extraction, initial screening of document classification, drafting reconciliation difference descriptions, and organizing statement notes and process documents; account determination, period attribution, characterizing differences, and the basis for external filing must still be handled by people.
Organization and finance team

Editorial task analysis: before introducing tools, clarify the links where they may be used, the knowledge scope and confidentiality requirements for accounting and payroll data, the approval authority for posting and adjustments, the checking and audit trail process for generated content, the error escalation path, and the responsible reviewer, so that any output returns to traceable ledger records.
Education and development

Editorial task analysis: focus training on accounting accounts and debit and credit logic, voucher and period determination, reconciliation and difference handling, internal control, and data confidentiality, and also train the habit of checking automatically recognized results and the awareness to escalate uncertain matters.

AI and accounting software can assist with extraction, comparison, and document drafts; specific account determination, approval, and filing are still handled according to personnel duties and authorization. BLS expects software automation to reduce staffing demand for this occupation and to increase analysis and consulting tasks, but it cannot be inferred from the fact that responsibility still rests with people that the number of positions will not decrease, nor should this projection be treated as a causal assessment of generative AI alone. items.title: What evidence employers usually look at

values: BK-01 problem statement and inputs

BK-01 is entirely editorially fictional; amounts are in yuan and the period is practice year April, and it involves neither value-added tax nor real accounting standard cases; record only according to the stated rules. Opening balances: bank deposits debit 10,000, accounts receivable debit 2,000, invested capital credit 12,000, and everything else 0. The accounts are only bank deposits, accounts receivable, prepaid expenses, accounts payable, invested capital, service revenue, rent expense, office expense, travel expense, and bank charges. Revenue is recognized in the month the service is completed; office materials are fully expensed in the month of purchase; next month's expense paid in advance is shown this month as an asset; each voucher is unique, and anything suspected of duplication or voucher error is first put on hold pending review without changing the original. The 12 materials: V01 4/02 completed service and received 3,000 in the bank; V02 4/03 completed service on credit 1,500; V03 4/05 collected 1,000 of the opening receivable into the bank; V04 4/07 the bank paid the month's rent of 800; V05 4/09 the bank paid 500 for office materials consumed this month; V06 4/12 purchased on credit and consumed 300 of office materials this month; V07 4/15 the bank repaid 200 owed to V06; V08 4/18 the bank prepaid 600 for May service fees; V09 4/22 travel of 400 for the month, a check was issued and the bank was deducted in the books, but the bank had not honored it by month end; V10 4/30 a service collection of 1,000 was completed, deposited in the bank, and recorded, and the bank did not enter the item until 5/01; V11 is a photocopy of the same transaction as V01, with the amount 3,000 and identical numbering and transaction, and is not recorded twice; V12 is an application for 700 in office expenses for the month, the amount has been altered and there is no reliable original, so it is returned first with a request for the issuing unit to reissue it, and it is not recorded in this problem's ledgers. The remaining V01—V10 have been reviewed and are complete in their basis.

April bank statement: opening 10,000; V01 +3,000, V03 +1,000, V04 -800, V05 -500, V07 -200, V08 -600, 4/30 bank charges -30 (formally notified by the bank and verified as genuine, not yet recorded in the books); closing 11,870. The statement does not include V09 and V10, and other bank records are correct. Paper or a spreadsheet and calculator are enough, and real accounts, personal data, and unit data are prohibited.

Editorial suggested timing: 60 minutes for judgments and entries in the first round, and 45 minutes for the trial balance and reconciliation in the second round; this may be extended according to learning progress and is not a hiring examination time limit.
Judgment steps and delivery

For V01—V12, write the period, the debit and credit accounts, the amount, or the reason for holding, transaction by transaction; deduplicate V11 and return V12, and do not force entries in order to make up 12 items. Post the valid V01—V10 and prepare a pre-adjustment trial balance; using the bank statement provided, list three kinds of difference: deposits in transit, outstanding checks, and the unrecorded bank charge.

Complete it independently before referring to the delivery: reconcile the bank and the books to the same balance, write the supplementary entry for the bank charge and the post-adjustment trial balance, and explain which items are timing differences that are not recorded separately and which must be recorded additionally under authorization.
Reference answer and review

Reference entries (debit / credit): V01 bank 3,000 / revenue 3,000; V02 receivable 1,500 / revenue 1,500; V03 bank 1,000 / receivable 1,000; V04 rent expense 800 / bank 800; V05 office expense 500 / bank 500; V06 office expense 300 / payable 300; V07 payable 200 / bank 200; V08 prepaid expense 600 / bank 600; V09 travel expense 400 / bank 400; V10 bank 1,000 / revenue 1,000; V11 is not recorded because it is a duplicate, and V12 is not recorded because the voucher amount is wrong and awaits reissue. V08 cannot be shown as an expense this month, and V06 must not be mistakenly written as a cash payment. Pre-adjustment balances: debit bank 12,500, receivable 2,500, prepaid 600, rent 800, office 800, travel 400; credit payable 100, invested capital 12,000, revenue 5,500; both sides 17,600. Reconciliation: bank 11,870 + deposits in transit 1,000 - outstanding checks 400 = 12,470; book 12,500 - unrecorded bank charges 30 = 12,470. V09 and V10 are already recorded and are listed only as timing differences in the reconciliation, with no second entry; the bank charge is debit bank charges 30 / credit bank 30, recorded additionally under the practice approval rules.

Post-adjustment balances: debit bank 12,470, receivable 2,500, prepaid 600, rent 800, office 800, travel 400, bank charges 30; credit payable 100, invested capital 12,000, revenue 5,500, both sides still 17,600. Check against these control figures first, then examine accounts, periods, and vouchers item by item; a balanced trial balance cannot reveal the duplicate V01 or the misposted V08, and the error notes and revision records must be kept.
Boundary of the exercise's use

All conditions are given; the only unknown is the learning problem you have not yet solved, and you may check yourself against the reference answer rather than skipping the question on the grounds that real business authorization is lacking. V12 is explicitly pending review, and there is no real voucher that can be fabricated. Real business must follow the applicable accounting system, review, and authority; this problem omits taxes, complex standards, and approvals and only tests debit and credit, periods, deduplication, and reconciliation logic, and it does not prove employment, qualification, or the ability to close the books independently.

Complete the judgments for the twelve BK-01 materials; V01—V10 are valid entries, V11 is a duplicate, and V12 awaits reissue, each handled separately. Output: a table of accounts, periods, debits and credits, and voucher status for each item; no real business materials are used.
Day four: entry and trial balance

Post the ten valid entries of BK-01 and list the pre-adjustment trial balance, calculating independently first and then checking the reference. Output: a trial balance with debit and credit totals of 17,600 and an account judgment note; a balance does not mean the business is correct.
Day five: bank reconciliation

Using the BK-01 bank statement, separate timing differences from the unrecorded bank charge, list the reconciliation on both sides, and record the bank charge additionally. Output: bank and books reconciled to 12,470, with the post-adjustment trial balance and notes on handling the three differences.
Day six: independent review

Review-type self-questioning: against the BK-01 reference answer, check the period of V08, the duplicate V11, and the voucher status of V12 transaction by transaction; teacher feedback is optional. Output: first-round errors, the basis for revisions, and the questions still to be studied, without fabricating external review.
Final review: decide whether to continue, pause, or change direction, and write clearly the basis and the parts that are still uncertain.
Output: a one-page decision statement with an evidence list.

entries: Continue exploring: you can complete BK-01 and explain the voucher status, the accounts, and the three differences, and you are willing to review item by item; this is only an exploratory signal, not proof of occupational competence gained in seven days.
Pause: you can complete the entry but find it hard to accept the correction of the basis through review, or are unwilling to invest time in item-by-item checking and audit trails.
Change direction: if you would rather do more focused work such as payroll accounting or billing settlement, you can compare payroll and timekeeping clerks and billing and posting clerks.
Verify authorization: if the target position involves closing or external filing, check the account set permissions and the approval process first.
Complete the evidence: organize the seven-day output into a reviewable accounting portfolio for a job interview or a course application.
Cost assessment: put course and examination fees, continuing education time, and software learning costs into a written plan.

Next step: based on the verification results, decide whether to first take basic accounting courses, first accumulate practical experience, or first enter a finance department through an adjacent position.

The U.S. BLS lists the typical entry-level education as some college, no degree, with moderate-term on-the-job training; employer requirements vary, some accept a high school diploma, and professional certification is usually not required. In the O*NET education question, 41% chose high school or equivalent, 21% chose a postsecondary certificate, and 12% chose a bachelor's degree; these are respondents' answers about the education required for the position, not the educational composition of workers or a uniform statutory threshold.

In mainland China, Article 4 of the Accounting Law (amended in 2024) makes the person in charge of the unit responsible for the truthfulness and completeness of the unit's accounting work and materials; Article 14 requires checking original vouchers, returning inaccurate or incomplete records for correction or supplementation, and requiring the issuing unit to reissue those with amount errors; Article 25 provides that bookkeeping, approval, handling, and custody of property duties are separated and mutually constrained; and Article 35 prohibits a cashier from concurrently serving as the checker, the keeper of accounting archives, or the registrar of revenue, expenditure, expense, and claims and debt accounts. Accounting personnel in mainland China must have the professional competence required by the position; the head of an accounting office or the accounting supervisor must additionally hold a professional technical position qualification at the accountant level or above, or have at least three years of experience in accounting work. Continuing education applies to those who hold an accounting professional technical qualification and to those who work in accounting without that qualification, starting in the year after obtaining the qualification or starting work; it is no fewer than 90 credits per year, with professional subjects generally no less than two-thirds, and the specific registration follows local rules.
